main_text.l: gumentis de tanto germine olim quid Tibi polliceri queas, colligere facile possis. Proinde huic Nepoti & Filio tuo hæc ipsa scribendi dicendiq; Pericula ut quàm studiosissimè commendata esse velis, impensè rogamus. Te namq; maximorum onerum mole, quæ solius Reip. causâ in te suscepisti, distractissimum, hisce legendis minimè vacare posse, libenter agnoscimus, certò nihilominus persuasi, hanc observantiæ nostræ humilem tesse-ram[?] Magnificentiæ T. haud ingratam futuram. Quâ fiducia freti supremum Numen assiduò invocamus, ut Te diu servet Electori Serenissimo FRIDERICO IV. Nutritio nostro clementissimo, Reip. Ecclesiæ, nobis. Ad S. Cyriacum in Vangionibus. Anno Christi Mediatoris ∞ IↃ CIX[?]. à.d. IV. Kall.Iulij.

page.notes: The first word "gumentis" is a fragment: the start of the word is cut off at the left edge of the printed line. The date is printed with the reversed-C numerals; the ∞ ornament before it is kept as printed and the reading "IↃ CIX" is marked doubtful. "tesse-ram" is a hyphenated word at a line end; the reading of the stem is doubtful. The greeting "Nobilitati" has a decorative initial N, copied as N.
